settled_prefix_audit.settled_definition: Every vertex in prefix P currently holds the unique token whose destination is that vertex.
settled_prefix_audit.proved_incompatibility: If P is settled, no token outside P can have its destination in P.
settled_prefix_audit.reason: The unique token destined for each z in P already occupies z; bijective occupancy prevents the same token from being outside P.

corrected_frontier_claim.preconditions: Earlier blocks B_1,...,B_(i-1) are settled; current block B_i is open; a token destined in B_i is currently in B_(i+2) or farther.
corrected_frontier_claim.claim_tested: The exact incoming token can be prepared to cross cut v_i v_(i+1) using at most one swap at v_(i+1) with one of its pendant leaves before crossing that cut.
corrected_frontier_claim.counterexample: Bare backbone v_1,...,v_t with leaves x at v_1 and y at v_t, only tokens at x,y exchanged; set i=1 and give v_2 no pendant leaves.
corrected_frontier_claim.scope: Refutes only one-hop local access; D=t+1 pays for the remote token travel and no unbounded approximation ratio follows.

input_data: For each token, source and destination vertices and their backbone block indices.
For every backbone cut, the exact left-to-right and right-to-left token identity sets; both have size r_i.
For each pendant edge, whether its leaf token must be loaded/unloaded.

fixed_pairing_lemma.statement: For a fixed bijective pairing of opposite-direction path tokens at every edge, a legal monotone schedule exists iff the directed crossing-event precedence graph is acyclic.
fixed_pairing_lemma.verification_complexity: Polynomial in the number of token-edge path incidences.
fixed_pairing_lemma.limitation: Searching edge pairings is not shown polynomial; a topological schedule may take sum_e r(e) singleton rounds and does not imply O(D+W_max).

identity_resolved_monotone_event_model.detour_classification: An actual swap event is extra if at least one swapped token crosses an edge absent from that token's unique source-destination path; this captures temporary displacement, including correctly placed tokens moved away and later returned.

forced_cycle_obstruction.permutation: Leaf tokens A,B,C route 1->2, 2->3, 3->1; center token Z is fixed.
forced_cycle_obstruction.conclusion: No monotone schedule exists; every valid schedule contains an off-path displacement or repeated path-edge crossing.
forced_cycle_obstruction.scope: Finite structural obstruction to monotone routing, not an asymptotic lower bound against constant-factor schedules.

universal_caterpillar_question.target: A deterministic polynomial-time matching schedule with R<=c*(D+W_max) for a universal constant c on all caterpillars.
universal_caterpillar_question.next_proof_obligation: Find a polynomially computable, token-realizable augmentation of the event DAG by extra crossings with matching-round schedule length O(D+W_max), or prove a parameterized lower bound ruling out the target.

prior_art_scope.source: Kawahara et al., The Time Complexity of Permutation Routing via Matching, Token Swapping and a Variant (JGAA 2019)
prior_art_scope.relevance: Gives an optimal polynomial algorithm for sequential token swapping on star-path graphs, a restricted caterpillar shape; this is not a matching-round bound.

prior_art_scope.source: Alon, Chung, Graham (1994), Routing Permutations on Graphs via Matchings
prior_art_scope.relevance: Classical matching-round model and worst-case tree routing bounds, not the instance-wise caterpillar target.

prior_art_scope.source: Aichholzer et al. (2022), Hardness of Token Swapping on Trees
prior_art_scope.relevance: Parallel token swapping hardness on general trees; does not settle this caterpillar subclass or bound.
